questions.context:
The first time I entered a cooking competition, I was sure I would lose. The other contestants were students from cooking schools, and I had only learned from my grandmother. But I decided to cook her famous apple pie — the recipe she had given me years before, written on a small card.

The competition hall was huge, with long tables and bright lights. When the clock started, my hands were shaking. I mixed the flour, cut the apples, and tried to remember my grandmother's voice: 'Cook with your heart, not with fear.' Slowly, I calmed down.

When the judges tasted my pie, one of them closed her eyes and smiled. Later, I learned that she had grown up eating the same kind of pie in her village. I didn't win first place — I came third — but the judges gave my pie a special mention for 'taste of home'.

My grandmother cried when I told her. The card with the recipe now hangs in my kitchen, and one day I will pass it to my own grandchildren.
questions.stem: Why was the writer surprised about entering the competition?
options: She thought she would win easily.
She didn't like the other contestants.
questions.explanation: She says she was sure she would lose because the others were from cooking schools.

tasks.title: Mock 2 · Part 1: Reply to Tom's email
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Tom. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
How was your summer? I've got great news — I passed all my exams!
Listen, I want to start learning photography. You're good at it — what camera should a beginner buy? Is it expensive?
Also, our school is starting a photography club. Would you be interested in joining it with me? We could meet on Fridays after school.
And one more thing — can you send me some of your best photos?
Write soon!
Tom
points: Give advice about a beginner camera and its price
Answer about joining the photography club
Say if you will send photos
tasks.model:
Hi Tom,

Great to hear from you, and congratulations on your exams! My summer was good — I spent most of it taking photos by the sea.

For a beginner, I think you should buy a simple second-hand camera. They are much cheaper than new ones — mine cost only fifty pounds, and it takes great photos.

I'd love to join the photography club with you! Fridays are perfect for me, because I finish school early that day.

Of course I'll send you some photos — I'll choose my best ones this weekend.

Best wishes,
Ivan
tasks.modelNotes: All four points answered; advice with should; enthusiastic, natural tone.
checklist: All four content points are answered
The email answers both questions about the club and photos

tasks.title: Mock 2 · Part 2: The best day of the year
tasks.rubric: Your school magazine asks students to write articles about their favourite day of the year. Write your article (about 100 words), saying what the day is, what you do, and why it is special.
points: Say who you spend it with
tasks.model:
The Best Day of the Year

What is your favourite day of the year? For me, it is easy — the first day of summer.

On that day, my family and I always drive to the lake near our village. We swim, have a picnic under the trees, and play cards until the evening. My uncle usually brings his guitar, and we sing together when the sun goes down.

I love this day because it feels like freedom. School is finished, the days are long, and everyone is happy and relaxed.

All in all, it isn't about what we do — it's about being together. That's why it's special.
tasks.modelNotes: Opens with a question to the reader, clear paragraphs, 'all in all' conclusion, personal feeling.

l_m2_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m2_p3_main.text: Hello everyone, and thank you for coming to today's information meeting about the City Half Marathon. My name is Diane, and I'm one of the organisers.

l_m2_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m2_p3_main.text: The race takes place on the twenty-second of September. It starts at nine o'clock in the morning in Central Park and finishes at the stadium near the river.

l_m2_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m2_p3_main.text: Runners can choose between two distances this year: ten kilometres for beginners, and the full half marathon of twenty-one kilometres for experienced runners.

l_m2_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m2_p3_main.text: Every runner receives a free T-shirt and a medal. The first three runners in each category also win prizes — this year they are sports shop gift cards worth up to two hundred pounds.

l_m2_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m2_p3_main.text: To enter, visit our website and pay the fifteen pound entry fee before the end of August. Last year, three thousand people took part, so don't wait too long! For questions, call us on zero-two-zero, seven-nine-four, six-six-three — that's 0207 946 663.

l_m2_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m2_p4_main.text: Good afternoon. Today I'm going to talk about my work as a mountain rescue volunteer. I've been doing this job for eight years, and people often ask me why I do it.

l_m2_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m2_p4_main.text: The truth is, it started with an accident. When I was nineteen, I got lost in the mountains during a snowstorm. A rescue team found me after ten hours — cold, tired, but alive. I promised myself that day that I would help others in the same way.

l_m2_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m2_p4_main.text: Being a rescue volunteer isn't easy. We train every weekend, whatever the weather, and we must be ready to leave our homes at any time — day or night. Last winter I was called out fourteen times. Sometimes we walk for hours in the dark with heavy equipment.

l_m2_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m2_p4_main.text: But the difficult moments are rare. Most of our work is helping people who are tired, or who took a wrong path. And when we find someone safe, the feeling is amazing. Last month we rescued a father and his daughter — their smiles were worth everything.

l_m2_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m2_p4_main.text: If you want to join us, you don't need to be an expert climber. You need fitness, teamwork, and the wish to help. Come and meet us — we meet every first Saturday of the month at the rescue centre.
